article_content: Nigerian officials have reported a devastating fuel truck accident that ignited into a massive inferno, claiming the lives of over 100 people, including numerous bus passengers, and destroying at least 12 vehicles. The tragedy occurred on Friday along the Onitsha-Enugu expressway in Anambra state's Oyi Council area. Authorities stated that the petroleum truck was navigating a section of the highway riddled with deep craters when it swerved sharply, overturned, and spilled its highly flammable contents across the roadway. Witnesses described the scene as apocalyptic, with the spilled fuel erupting into a colossal fire that engulfed multiple vehicles, including the truck and several buses. Nigerian media outlets quoted horrified bystanders who recounted the harrowing screams of those trapped inside the burning vehicles, pleading for help that never arrived. Nigeria's roads are notoriously perilous, often likened to death traps due to their decrepit condition, poorly maintained vehicles, and reckless driving practices. The Federal Road Safety Commission's operations head, Ben Ekenna, issued a stark warning, stating that such disasters will continue unabated unless drastic measures are taken to address the country's deteriorating infrastructure. Officials estimate that over 6,000 lives are lost annually in traffic-related incidents across Nigeria, though many believe the true toll could be significantly higher due to underreporting in remote areas.

Le autorità hanno dichiarato che l'autocisterna del carburante stava percorrendo un tratto di autostrada pieno di enormi buche quando ha sterzato bruscamente, si è ribaltata e ha sparso il suo contenuto altamente infiammabile sulla carreggiata. article_content: CAIRO - Egyptian armed forces chief Field Marshal Abdel Fattah el-Sissi has given the clearest signal yet that he will run for president, saying he cannot ignore the demands of the 'majority', Egypt's state news agency reported on Tuesday. El-Sissi, who led the ousting of Egypt's first freely elected president, Mohamed Morsi, said 'official procedures' concerning his candidacy were expected in the coming days. El-Sissi, widely expected to win the presidency of the Arab world's most populous country, was speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Cairo war college. Most Egyptians regard him as a decisive figure who can end the political turmoil that has gripped Egypt since a popular uprising toppled autocratic president Hosni Mubarak in 2011. In his speech, el-Sissi said Egypt was witnessing difficult times that required the unity of the people, army, and police, according to the state news agency MENA.

El-Sissi, che ha guidato il rovesciamento del primo presidente egiziano eletto a suffragio universale, Mohamed Morsi, ha dichiarato che 'le procedure ufficiali' relative alla sua candidatura sarebbero state annunciate nei prossimi giorni. El-Sissi, ampiamente atteso a vincere la presidenza del paese più popoloso del mondo arabo, parlava durante una cerimonia di laurea al college di guerra del Cairo. La maggior parte degli egiziani lo considera una figura decisa che possa porre fine al tumulto politico che ha colpito l'Egitto dal 2011, quando un'insurrezione popolare ha rovesciato il presidente autocratico Hosni Mubarak. article_content: MOSCOW - FIFA charged World Cup host Russia with fan racism Tuesday, less than two months before the tournament begins. Disputed chants were aimed at black French players, including Paul Pogba, during France's 3-1 friendly win over Russia in St. Petersburg last month. "Disciplinary proceedings have been opened against the Russian Football Union for this incident," FIFA said. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Arkady Dvorkovich, who is overseeing World Cup preparations, told state news agencies Tuesday that Russia was 'monitoring the situation' of racist fans. "We're taking measures to address these isolated incidents," he said. "But if that happens... there should be zero tolerance for these people." The RFU said it is cooperating with the FIFA investigation. "A request has been made to the Interior Ministry to identify several persons who were involved in these incidents," RFU anti-discrimination officer Alexei Smertin was quoted as saying Monday by the Tass news agency. "If these people's guilt is proven, then there's a high likelihood they won't be allowed to attend World Cup and Russian league games." Russia was previously charged with racist behavior by its fans at the last two European Championships. On both occasions, the RFU addressed the issue. It's the third racism case this season at St. Petersburg Stadium, which will host a World Cup semifinal match. Zenit St. Petersburg has twice faced UEFA charges for racism by its fans in Europa League games. Zenit fans flew a banner praising convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic when playing a Macedonian club in November and are accused of using a racially charged term to mock an injured black player in a game against Leipzig. The second case is due to be heard by UEFA on May 31, two weeks before the World Cup begins.

Canti contestati sono stati rivolti a giocatori neri francesi, tra cui Paul Pogba, durante la vittoria amichevole della Francia per 3-1 contro la Russia a San Pietroburgo lo scorso mese. "Sono stati avviati procedimenti disciplinari contro l'Unione del Calcio Russa per questo incidente," ha dichiarato la FIFA. Il vice-primo ministro russo Arkady Dvorkovich, responsabile della preparazione del Mondiale, ha detto agli organi di stampa di stato martedì che la Russia stava 'monitorando la situazione' di tifosi razzisti. "Stiamo adottando misure per affrontare questi incidenti isolati," ha detto. "Ma se dovesse accadere... non dovrebbe esserci tolleranza per queste persone." L'Unione del Calcio Russa ha dichiarato di collaborare con l'inchiesta della FIFA. "É stata fatta richiesta al Ministero dell'Interno per identificare diverse persone coinvolte in questi incidenti," ha dichiarato Alexei Smertin, responsabile anti-discriminazione dell'Unione del Calcio Russa, citato lunedì dall'agenzia di stampa Tass. "Se viene provata la colpevolezza di queste persone, c'è una forte probabilità che non saranno ammessi ai Mondiali e alle partite della lega russa." La Russia era stata precedentemente accusata di comportamento razzista da parte dei suoi tifosi nelle ultime due edizioni del Campionato Europeo. In entrambe le occasioni, l'Unione del Calcio Russa ha affrontato la questione. Si tratta del terzo caso di razzismo questa stagione allo Stadio di San Pietroburgo, che ospiterà una semifinale del Mondiale. Lo Zenit San Pietroburgo ha già affrontato due volte accuse dell'UEFA per razzismo da parte dei suoi tifosi in partite di Europa League. I tifosi dello Zenit hanno esposto uno striscione in onore del criminale di guerra condannato Ratko Mladic durante una partita contro un club macedone nel novembre scorso ed è accusato di aver usato un termine a connotazione razziale per deridere un giocatore nero ferito in una partita contro il Leipzig. Il secondo caso sarà esaminato dall'UEFA il 31 maggio, due settimane prima dell'inizio del Mondiale.

article_content: Myanmar’s parliament announced Tuesday that Htin Kyaw has assumed the presidency without an official vote. As a close ally of National League for Democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, Htin Kyaw, though not a parliament member, played a significant role in Tuesday’s historic transition. Here is what is widely known about Htin Kyaw: A longtime and trusted associate of Aung San Suu Kyi, he is recognized internationally for his leadership qualities. His educational journey began in 1962 at a renowned high school attended by Aung San Suu Kyi. By 1963, he pursued university studies in arts, leading to a degree in economics with a statistics focus by 1968. In 1970, he joined a computer center as an analyst. The following year, he furthered his education in computer science in London. Htin Kyaw, son of the respected literary figure Min Thu Wun, boasts a strong academic background. In 1973, he married Daw Su Su Lwin, a prominent figure in the Foreign Relations Committee. In 1974, he pursued advanced computer studies in Tokyo and later earned a master’s in computer science. From 1975, he held various government roles, including positions in industrial and economic planning. In 1987, he attended management training in the U.S. He resigned from government service in 1992. In 2000, he was briefly detained for political activism. By 2012, he joined the executive committee of Daw Khin Kyi Foundation, focusing on education and health. Aung San Suu Kyi emphasized Htin Kyaw's loyalty, discipline, and educational background, deeming him fit for national leadership. This biography is compiled by the Daw Khin Kyi Foundation, established in 2012 to honor Aung San Suu Kyi's late mother.

Come stretto alleato del leader della Lega Nazionale per la Democrazia, Aung San Suu Kyi, Htin Kyaw, sebbene non sia un membro del parlamento, ha avuto un ruolo significativo nella storica transizione di martedì. Ecco cosa è ampiamente noto su Htin Kyaw: un lungimirante e fidato associato di Aung San Suu Kyi, riconosciuto a livello internazionale per le sue qualità di leadership. Il suo percorso formativo è iniziato nel 1962 in una rinomata scuola superiore frequentata da Aung San Suu Kyi. Nel 1963 ha proseguito gli studi universitari in arte, conseguendo una laurea in economia con concentrazione in statistica entro il 1968. L'anno successivo si è unito a un centro informatico come analista. L'anno dopo ha proseguito gli studi in informatica a Londra. Htin Kyaw, figlio del rispettato figura letteraria Min Thu Wun, vanta una solida formazione accademica. Nel 1973 si è sposato con Daw Su Su Lwin, una figura prominente nel Comitato per le Relazioni Esteri. Nel 1974 ha proseguito gli studi avanzati in informatica a Tokyo e in seguito ha conseguito un master in scienze informatiche. Dal 1975 ha ricoperto vari ruoli governativi, tra cui posizioni nella pianificazione industriale ed economica. Nel 1987 ha frequentato un corso di gestione negli Stati Uniti. Si è dimesso dal servizio governativo nel 1992. Nel 2000 è stato brevemente trattenuto per attivismo politico. Nel 2012 si è unito al comitato esecutivo della Fondazione Daw Khin Kyi, concentrandosi su istruzione e salute. Aung San Suu Kyi ha enfatizzato la lealtà, la disciplina e il background accademico di Htin Kyaw, considerandolo adatto alla leadership nazionale. Questa biografia è stata compilata dalla Fondazione Daw Khin Kyi, istituita nel 2012 per onorare la defunta madre di Aung San Suu Kyi, Daw Khin Kyi.

article_content: Britain's Foreign Minister Jeremy Hunt tweeted Thursday that Myanmar officials should face accountability for their country's Rohingya crisis before the International Criminal Court. Hunt's comments, referring to Myanmar as Burma, followed his meeting with embattled Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi during a high-profile state visit. The visit came after Tuesday's release of a United Nations report criticizing Suu Kyi's handling of the crisis. The report outlines why Myanmar generals should be prosecuted for alleged human rights abuses against the Rohingya minority. It also accuses military leaders of extrajudicial killings, rape, and razing Rohingya villages in Rakhine, forcing over 1.2 million Rohingya to flee to neighboring Bangladesh. Hunt arrived in Yangon Wednesday for a two-day visit. He planned to meet with military and civilian leaders. In Naypyidaw, he met with Aung San Suu Kyi, who agreed to consider crisis-related issues, including the case of two Reuters journalists sentenced to 7-year prison terms earlier this month.

I commenti di Hunt, che si riferivano al Myanmar come Burma, sono seguiti al suo incontro con la leader del Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi, durante una visita di Stato di alto profilo. La visita è avvenuta dopo la pubblicazione martedì di un rapporto delle Nazioni Unite che critica la gestione della crisi da parte di Suu Kyi. Il rapporto dettaglia perché i generali del Myanmar dovrebbero essere perseguiti per presunti abusi dei diritti umani contro la minoranza Rohingya. Si accusano inoltre i leader militari di uccisioni extragiudiziali, stupri e distruzione di villaggi Rohingya nello Stato Rakhine, costringendo oltre 1,2 milioni di Rohingya a fuggire nel vicino Bangladesh. Hunt è arrivato a Yangon mercoledì per una visita di due giorni. Aveva pianificato di incontrare leader militari e civili. A Naypyidaw, ha incontrato Aung San Suu Kyi, che ha accettato di considerare questioni relative alla crisi, tra cui il caso di due giornalisti di Reuters condannati a 7 anni di prigione all'inizio del mese.

article_content: A Japanese man was arrested on Thursday after intentionally crashing a car through a barrier near the Israeli embassy in Tokyo, police said. Mor Eliyahu, a spokeswoman for the Israeli embassy, told AFP that the incident 'is suspected to be a premeditated vehicle ramming attack, and it is currently under investigation by local police.' The suspect, identified as Shinobu Sekiguchi, 53, is believed to have links to a right-wing group known for its anti-Semitic views. Police made no comment on the possible motives of the unemployed man, but sources suggest the incident may have been inspired by recent global tensions. The man drove his small car through the barrier into a fence at an intersection around 100 meters from the embassy, narrowly missing the embassy's main entrance. One police officer was seriously injured in the incident late Thursday morning. 'At around 10:55 am, the suspect, driving a minicar, suddenly turned to the left and rammed into a male police officer in his 20s who was patrolling for the Israeli embassy,' a police spokesperson told AFP. The suspect's affiliation with the right-wing group, which has been vocal about its opposition to Israel, raises concerns about the incident being part of a larger coordinated effort. Media also reported that the man had previously expressed anti-Semitic sentiments online. A fire department spokesperson said only that they received an emergency call and gave no further details. 'Around 11:00 am, I heard a huge bang, so I went outside to check. Then I saw a policeman injured and in pain near the traffic barrier, and it looked like he was bleeding heavily. There was also a black car parked nearby,' a restaurant employee working nearby told public broadcaster NHK. Countries around the world have stepped up security around Israeli diplomatic missions since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas last month. On October 21, four people were arrested after a pipe bomb exploded near the Israeli embassy in Cyprus, causing little damage but raising alarms about potential threats. On October 14, an employee of the Israeli embassy in China was attacked in Beijing. A foreign suspect was arrested, and authorities have not provided further details. There has also been a sharp rise in anti-Semitic as well as Islamophobic incidents worldwide. Israel launched an offensive in Gaza in retaliation for Hamas's brutal October 7 attacks, which killed 1,200 people, most of them civilians. With the Hamas-run health ministry claiming the death toll from the Israeli offensive has now topped 11,500, including thousands of children, calls for a truce are mounting.

article_content:
U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry is joining foreign ministers from European and Arab nations Monday in Paris for urgent talks on the escalating battle against Islamic State and efforts to enforce an immediate political resolution to the crisis in Syria.

Diplomats are racing to build momentum for a critical meeting Friday in New York that would include U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon and his envoy for Syria, Staffan de Mistura. They aim to establish a framework for a cease-fire and political process based on the international agreement reached last month in Vienna to begin peace talks by January 1.

The push toward negotiations is the most significant in nearly two years since two rounds of U.N.-brokered peace talks collapsed in early 2014 without progress.

Since then, what began as a number of opposition and militant groups fighting largely against the government of President Bashar al-Assad has grown more complex with the rise of the Islamic State group and its seizure of large areas in eastern Syria and northern and western Iraq.

Italy's Foreign Minister Paolo Gentiloni (C), U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry (L), and UN special envoy for Libya Martin Kobler at a joint news conference following an international conference on Libya at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Rome, Dec. 13, 2015.

The result has been a multi-faceted conflict with various groups fighting each other for territory, as well as the introduction last year of a U.S.-led coalition conducting airstrikes against Islamic State and, in September, Russian forces launching their own air campaign.

The fighting that began in March 2011 has left more than 240,000 people dead and forced more than 11 million people from their homes, including a large influx who have sought safety in Europe, forcing governments there to scramble to respond.

Kerry will travel Tuesday to Russia for meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Sergei Lavrov for further talks on progressing the political track in Syria as well as fighting Islamic State.

I diplomatici stanno correndo per costruire slancio verso un incontro critico venerdì a New York, che includerà il Segretario Generale delle Nazioni Unite, Ban Ki-moon, e il suo inviato per la Siria, Staffan de Mistura. L'obiettivo è stabilire una cornice per un cessate il fuoco e un processo politico basato sull'accordo internazionale raggiunto lo scorso mese a Vienna per avviare colloqui di pace entro il 1° gennaio.

La spinta verso i negoziati è la più significativa da quasi due anni, dall'effondramento di due round di colloqui di pace sotto l'egida delle Nazioni Unite all'inizio del 2014, senza progressi.

Da allora, ciò che iniziò come una serie di gruppi di opposizione e miliziani che combattevano principalmente contro il governo del Presidente Bashar al-Assad è diventato più complesso con l'ascesa del gruppo Stato Islamico e la sua conquista di ampie aree nella Siria orientale e in Iraq settentrionale e occidentale.

Il Ministro degli Esteri italiano, Paolo Gentiloni (C), il Segretario di Stato degli Stati Uniti, John Kerry (L), e l'inviato speciale delle Nazioni Unite per la Libia, Martin Kobler, durante una conferenza stampa congiunta a seguito di una conferenza internazionale sulla Libia presso il Ministero degli Affari Esteri a Roma, il 13 dicembre 2015.

Il risultato è stato un conflitto multiforme, con vari gruppi che si combattono per territorio, oltre all'introduzione, lo scorso anno, di una coalizione guidata dagli Stati Uniti che conducerebbero attacchi aerei contro l'ISIS e, lo scorso settembre, delle forze russe che hanno avviato la loro campagna aerea.

I combattimenti iniziati nel marzo 2011 hanno lasciato più di 240.000 persone uccise e hanno costretto oltre 11 milioni di persone a lasciare le loro case, tra cui un grande afflusso di persone che hanno cercato sicurezza in Europa, costringendo i governi europei a reagire.

Kerry viaggerà mercoledì in Russia per incontri con il Presidente russo Vladimir Putin e Sergei Lavrov per ulteriori discussioni sul progresso del percorso politico in Siria e sulla lotta all'ISIS.

article_content: Struggling in the polls, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud Party has escalated its attacks on Benny Gantz, falsely claiming the former military chief is mentally unfit for office. A new series of video ads distorts Gantz's public appearances, inaccurately suggesting instability and editing in eerie sound effects from the movie 'Psycho' to reinforce their baseless claims. The videos have been widely condemned as a desperate and unethical smear campaign. Recent polls show Gantz's Blue and White party significantly ahead of Likud, prompting Netanyahu's increasingly aggressive tactics. The prime minister has also resorted to fearmongering about Arab voters, continuing his pattern of divisiveness. Netanyahu faces multiple corruption investigations, and his inability to stop Gaza rocket attacks has further eroded public confidence. His campaign falsely claims Gantz was 'treated by a psychologist' and 'prescribed medication,' allegations Gantz denies, stating he consulted only with a military advisor. Retired generals, including former air force chief Amir Eshel, have come to Gantz's defense, calling Netanyahu's attacks dishonorable. The Israel Psychology Association has condemned the use of mental health 'as a political weapon,' emphasizing that seeking counseling is a sign of strength, not weakness.

article_content: Chevron has fully resumed operations at the Tamar field, a critical offshore natural gas facility, following explicit authorization from the Israeli government. 'We have resumed natural gas supplies to our customers in Israel and across the region from the Tamar Production Platform,' Chevron stated on Monday. The platform, located just a few miles away from Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea, was forced to halt production on October 9 by Israel's Ministry of Energy, two days after the Hamas attack on the country. As one of Israel's main offshore natural gas facilities, the Tamar field accounted for over 70% of the nation's electricity generation in 2022. The resumption of production has led to a significant increase in natural gas exports to Egypt. A Bloomberg report released Monday showed gas inflows rising sharply to 350-450 million cubic feet per day, up from around 250 million earlier this month. However, the current rate remains well below pre-conflict levels. Before October 7, Egypt imported nearly 1 billion cubic meters of natural gas daily from Israel. Egypt, which has recently faced supply shortages, is committed to a memorandum of understanding signed after Russia's invasion of Ukraine to export Israeli liquefied natural gas to European markets, a move that could strengthen Europe's energy independence from Russia.

'Abbiamo ripreso i rifornimenti di gas naturale ai nostri clienti in Israele e nel resto della regione dalla piattaforma di produzione di Tamar,' ha dichiarato lunedì Chevron. La piattaforma, ubicata a poche miglia da Gaza nel Mar Mediterraneo, è stata costretta a sospendere la produzione il 9 ottobre dal Ministero dell'Energia israeliano, due giorni dopo l'attacco di Hamas al paese. Il campo di Tamar, una delle principali strutture offshore per il gas naturale di Israele, ha coperto oltre il 70% della produzione di elettricità nazionale nel 2022. La ripresa della produzione ha comportato un significativo aumento delle esportazioni di gas naturale verso l'Egitto. Un rapporto di Bloomberg pubblicato lunedì ha riscontrato un incremento considerevole degli afflussi, che sono passati da 250 milioni a 350-450 milioni di piedi cubi al giorno. Tuttavia, l'attuale tasso remains ancora al di sotto del 50% rispetto ai livelli precedenti al conflitto. Prima del 7 ottobre, l'Egitto importava quasi 1 miliardo di metri cubi di gas naturale al giorno da Israele. L'Egitto, che ha recentemente affrontato carenze di approvvigionamento, è vincolato da un memorandum d'intesa firmato dopo l'invasione russa dell'Ucraina per esportare gas naturale liquefatto israeliano nei mercati europei, una mossa che potrebbe rafforzare l'indipendenza energetica dell'Europa dalla Russia.

article_content: Turkey and Israel are on the brink of a severe diplomatic crisis following the revelation that Israeli security forces intentionally targeted nine Turkish citizens aboard a humanitarian vessel attempting to deliver aid to Gaza last year. The highly anticipated United Nations report, set to be released this Friday, is expected to confirm Israel's culpability in the attack. Turkish Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan has issued an ultimatum: Israel must apologize, provide substantial compensation to the victims' families, and lift the oppressive blockade on Gaza for relations to improve. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has defiantly refused to acknowledge any wrongdoing, intensifying the standoff. The breakdown in relations between the once-strong allies has triggered concerns among global powers, particularly the United States, which has been attempting to mediate the dispute. Turkish Foreign Minister Ahmet Davutoglu has signalled that Turkey is prepared to impose significant sanctions on Israel, with international relations expert Soli Ozel suggesting that Turkey could reduce diplomatic ties and pursue legal action against Israeli officials. Meanwhile, columnist Semih Idiz notes that Turkey's growing influence in the Middle East has emboldened its stance, making it less dependent on maintaining good relations with Israel. Despite the political tensions, bilateral trade remains robust, with Turkey continuing to rely on Israel for critical military equipment, such as drones. However, political columnist Asla Aydintasbas warns that Erdogan's strong position on the issue leaves little room for compromise, as the Turkish public remains deeply offended by Israel's actions. The upcoming UN report has set a deadline for resolution, with diplomatic efforts expected to intensify in the coming days to prevent further escalation.

Nel frattempo, il commentatore Semih Idiz nota che l'influenza crescente della Turchia in Medio Oriente ha rafforzato la sua posizione, rendendola meno dipendente dal mantenimento dei buoni rapporti con Israele.
